objective: Audit the v0.5.1 internal problem-reporting, owner triage, immutable fix release, managed update, and synchronized component-map lifecycle without expanding the evidence beyond the observed environments.

elements.target: The accepted component map uses the canonical skills/ package path and covers reporting, owner API, issue-to-release, and managed-update elements without dropping unrelated components.

evidence.observed: Candidate component-map-1153ef523720 was accepted; the immediate follow-up returned checked_unchanged with no changes.
Canonical managed package/update elements and four problem-reporting lifecycle elements are accepted.

elements.safe_interpretation: The formal structural authority now matches the active package/reporting architecture and preserves the other mapped research components.

elements.target: Exactly one GitHub CLI-discoverable package exists under skills/analyze-project-claims, with synchronized version and manifest identity.

evidence.observed: Repository and installed package manifests verified; native registry returned exactly one canonical user-scope unpinned v0.5.1 installation.
The package contract requires the reporter, schemas, update helper, and one canonical skills/ tree.

elements.safe_interpretation: The observed repository and managed Windows installation have one consistent v0.5.1 package identity.

elements.target: A separately consented updater delegates replacement to GitHub CLI and verifies source, scope, pin, version, tree, and package integrity for next use.

evidence.observed: Installed v0.4.2 updated to v0.5.0 and installed v0.5.0 updated to v0.5.1, each with UPDATED_NEXT_USE.
Consent, binding, pinned/project degradation, local edits, postcondition, output bounds, locking, and lease tests passed.
Manifest, registry identity, dry-run no-op, NOT_DUE lease, and fresh Codex v0.5.1 activation were observed on Windows.

elements.safe_interpretation: The managed replacement path worked twice on the observed Windows host and is regression-tested across CI platforms; live replacement on other hosts remains unobserved.
elements.required_repair: Repeat live installed replacement and fresh-host activation on supported macOS and Linux hosts before making a cross-platform live-update claim.

elements.target: Problem reporting has a strict policy independent from update consent and defaults to local preview plus exact-report approval.

evidence.observed: The installed reporter in ask mode prepared a local preview with consent_required=true before issue delivery.

evidence.locator: default consent, off, ask, and auto-minimal paths
evidence.observed: Nine reporter regressions passed, including exact policy schema and non-storage of API tokens.

elements.safe_interpretation: The tested CLI paths keep update and reporting consent separate and require exact-report approval by default.

elements.target: Only fixed internal events and bounded diagnostics can be delivered; project content, arbitrary fields, paths, secrets, prompts, raw logs, and attachments are excluded.

evidence.observed: Issue #1 body matched the approved fixed-schema preview and contained no project content or attachments.

evidence.locator: schema, redaction, tamper, and argument-array regressions
evidence.observed: Unknown fields, modified fingerprints, secrets, absolute paths, and control characters were rejected.

elements.safe_interpretation: The tested reporter and observed issue enforce the bounded internal-event contract; absence of every possible secret format is not proved.

elements.target: The optional owner API authenticates scoped principals, isolates tenants, deduplicates, triages, retains, and deletes bounded reports without exposing database access.

evidence.observed: A local process E2E completed configure, consented submit, receive, status, delete, and not-found postcondition.
Eight authentication, tenant isolation, deduplication, triage, deletion, retention, schema, and rate-limit tests passed.

elements.safe_interpretation: The local standard-library service satisfies the tested contract; production HTTPS, storage encryption, backup, operations, and abuse resistance remain untested.
elements.required_repair: Deploy behind production HTTPS with encrypted persistent storage, monitoring, backup/restore testing, token rotation, and an external security review before production use.

elements.target: A report remains untrusted triage input until a red test, reviewed fix, commit-bound CI, immutable release, installed postcondition, and fresh-host activation complete.

evidence.observed: Issue #1 was received, triaged, reproduced by a failing test, fixed in CI-passing immutable v0.5.1, installed, activated in a fresh Codex host, then closed.
The owner workflow forbids executing issue text and requires regression, CI, new SemVer release, installed evidence, then closure.

elements.safe_interpretation: One owner-account private-repository issue completed the gated loop; independent-customer delivery and GitHub notification arrival remain unobserved.
elements.required_repair: Repeat with a separate authorized user account and directly observe the configured owner notification channel before claiming independent-user notification delivery.

strongest_safe_claim: Version 0.5.1 implements a separately consented bounded internal-report path, a locally tested tenant-isolated owner API, and one observed private GitHub issue-to-tested-release-to-installed-update loop on Windows; the synchronized accepted map and deterministic tests support these bounded claims.
claim_boundary: Production API security, GitHub notification arrival, independent-customer permissions, cross-platform live replacement, and general product reliability remain unproved.
unresolved_uncertainties: No production HTTPS API deployment or external security review has been observed.
No independent customer account or GitHub web/email/mobile notification delivery has been observed.
Live installed replacement and fresh-host activation were observed only on one Windows host.
The private repository still lacks an owner-approved software license.
